key_insight: An LLM-powered bariatric surgery education app (BariBot) was feasible to use postoperatively and was rated highly usable and acceptable by patients.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI chat tools may support patient education between clinical encounters, but they should complement—rather than replace—clinician guidance.
method: Prospective, single-arm mixed-methods feasibility study at a tertiary academic medical center.
Adult bariatric surgery patients used BariBot independently on postoperative day 1.
Usability measured with the System Usability Scale (SUS) plus post-use semi-structured interviews.
evidence_signal: Sixteen patients completed the study; there were no technical failures or early discontinuations, and the median SUS score was 91.3, indicating excellent perceived usability.
watch_item: Findings are based on a small, single-center, short-term study, so safety and effectiveness during longer unsupervised use remain unproven.
paper_title: Evaluation of an AI-Powered Patient Education Application in Bariatric Surgery: A Prospective Mixed-Methods Feasibility Study
